newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurotunnel - Key developments in troubled history.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel - Key developments in troubled history.

text.p: Eurotunnel on Thursday faced a crucial vote of its shareholders on a debt restructuring plan.

The company needs the approval of holders of two-thirds of the French shares and three-quarters of the British shares to pursue the deal struck in April to ease the crushing debt-servicing burden on the company.
Following is a chronology of the financial history of Eurotunnel, operator of the Channel Tunnel linking France and Britain.

July 10, 1997 - Holders of 920 million Eurotunnel shares vote at extraordinary general meeting on 70 billion franc ($11.7 billion) debt restructuring deal reached by Eurotunnel and its banks in April.
Approval of two-thirds of French shareholders and 75 percent of British shareholders is required.

July 1, 1997 - French finance ministry says France and Britain are prepared to extend Eurotunnel's operating licence to 99 years from 65, a move seen boosting the company's prospects and chances for shareholder approval of the restructuring plan.
June 24, 1997 - Extraordinary general meeting called for a vote on the debt plan is cancelled and rescheduled for July 10 due to lack of quorum after small shareholders shun the meeting.
June 15, 1997 - Freight services resume after repairs to damage caused by fire on November 18, 1996.
May 29, 1997 - Eurotunnel presents debt restructuring prospectus. Company forecasts profit in 2005, dividend in 2006, under "base scenario" assuming debt plan is approved.
May 16, 1997 - Arson suspected as most likely cause of 1996 fire, say sources close to the British side of the inquiry.
April 24, 1997 - Eurotunnel and lead banks agree on debt rescheduling plan covering 70 billion francs of junior debt.
Deal leaves shareholders with the right to 54.5 percent of long-term potential profits. It requires the approval of a majority of shareholders and all creditors.
Eurotunnel posts net loss of 6.1 billion francs for 1996.
November 18, 1996 - Fire breaks out in one of the two traffic tunnels. Thirty-four people evacuated; eight taken to hospital suffering from smoke inhalation, minor injuries.
October 24, 1996 - After more than a year of talks, Eurotunnel and lead bank lenders agree in principle on plan to reschedule 70 billion francs of junior debt.
February 12, 1996 - Paris court names two French and British former cabinet ministers to mediate debt talks between Eurotunnel and its bankers.
November 7, 1995 - Channel Tunnel welcomes its millionth motorist customer.
September 14, 1995 - Eurotunnel stops paying interest on its 62 billion franc bank debt, seeks help from France and Britain.
April 10, 1995 - Eurotunnel co-chairmen caution in joint statement, "Our debt service costs may overwhelm us".
February 17, 1995 - Eurotunnel loses court battle against EU decision to allow duty-free sales until 1999. Eurotunnel argues that the decision represents a huge subsidy for ferry companies.
February 10, 1995 - Eurotunnel says 1994 revenues of 30.6 million sterling well below target.
December 22, 1994 - Eurotunnel begins "Le Shuttle" train service running passengers and their cars.
November 14, 1994 - Eurotunnel begins Paris-London Eurostar high-speed passenger rail service.
May 26, 1994 - Eurotunnel raises 816 million sterling in share issue, adds credit facilities for 693 million pounds in refinancing deal.
May 19, 1994 - Eurotunnel begins freight service.
May 6, 1994 - Queen Elizabeth and President Francois Mitterrand formally open the Channel tunnel.
May 3, 1994 - Cost of Channel Tunnel construction estimated at 10 billion pounds -- more than double original estimate.
April 21, 1994. Eurotunnel says needs more cash and announces new delays in start of various services.
February 26, 1994 - Eurotunnel celebrates completion of project -- nearly a year behind schedule due to cost overruns.
December 1, 1990 - British worker Graham Fagg shakes hands with French counterpart Philippe Cozette through a gap in the service tunnel reached three years after start of tunnelling.
November 27, 1987 - Eurotunnel shares floated at 350 pence in London and 35 francs in Paris.

January 20, 1986 - Eurotunnel rail tunnel project is chosen, beating out plans for road/rail tunnel, road bridge between artificial islands and road bridge enclosed in a circular tube supported by giant pylons anchored to the sea floor.
September 11, 1981 - French President Francois Mitterrand and British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher agree to study tunnel. Thatcher insists on private sector financing.
1975 - Britain halts tunnel project due to spiralling costs.

1971 - Digging begins after 1964 agreement between France and Britain to build a subsea tunnel, an idea under discussion since the mid-18th century. Advocates include Napoleon. ($ = 5.959 French Francs)
